mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: labor market shock or recession risk
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE first exceeds 6.0% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for cyclicals and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during three-month INDPRO declines (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate regime that erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive acceleration in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) over two consecutive months signals improved consumer purchasing power, which boosts demand for goods and services and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth (month-over-month) increases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth accelerates for two consecutive months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent fall in both UNRATE and PAYEMS (below their 12-month averages) signals a dual labor market shock of rising unemployment and falling employment, which reduces aggregate demand and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE and PAYEMS fall below their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-mo avg for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its 12-month average for four consecutive months (p > 0.10).
